name: desktop-verification-port
goal: Give each verified browser run its own port while honoring overrides and refusing foreign servers

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Strict 22befc280 failed browser-error-evidence because another task owned 5797; verification ignored HARNESS_DESKTOP_TEST_PORT. No foreign server or user session was stopped.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: test-preview-refusal exercised only ordinary previews. Extend the same cold public/owner and real foreign-server refusal matrix to verified runs.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Sealed b4b3e0c9 at eb9868ed5: the cold verified configuration chooses 5797 instead of its named owned port; ordinary mode and foreign-server refusal pass.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: Both browser modes honor explicit ports, otherwise select a free loopback port. The static fixture receives that same port; existing-server refusal remains enabled.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: Sealed 527eff29 red and 2dc43319 green at 62a3f47f3: unchanged four-case ownership matrix proves both modes use the named port and refuse foreign content.

steps.title: Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
